Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.24% today after gaining nearly 13% over the past two weeks, riding a sharp rally in crude oil prices driven by geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Brent crude has spiked above $110 a barrel this week as Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing U.S. crude to around $102—a meaningful move for a refiner whose profitability depends on the spread between crude costs and refined product prices. With refineries running at 93.5% capacity and diesel storage low at 102.6 million barrels, tight supply conditions are working in the refiner's favor.

The recent rally also reflects tightening physical oil markets—tanker rates have surged enough that the actual cost to deliver crude is running about $38 per barrel higher than the headline price, effectively boosting margins for refiners who can move product. Trump's stated reluctance to use nuclear weapons or ground troops against Iran may have also eased some extreme risk premium out of the market, allowing the recent spike to stabilize rather than climb further.
